statement: The transformation of East Francia into the Holy Roman Empire occurred with Otto I's coronation as Emperor by Pope John XII (February 2, 962). Otto had already demonstrated imperial-scale authority by defeating the Magyars at Lechfeld (955) and was the undisputed dominant ruler of Latin Christendom. The imperial coronation linked his Frankish-German kingdom to the Roman imperial tradition and the papacy — creating a relationship that would generate centuries of conflict. The 'Holy Roman Empire of the German Nation' (the full title became standard in the 15th century) preserved Carolingian imperial ideology in a German institutional framework until 1806.
